subject: Territory-bound routing & scrub process — evidence needs
messages:
From: Claire Barnes <claire@finregcorp.com>

Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-18T09:28:00-07:00
Subject: Territory-bound routing & scrub process — initial questions

Vanessa,

Thanks for the time last week. A few follow-ups from our security review for FinReg's Dedicated deployment:

- We need confirmation that tenant data (including backups, snapshots, and ephemeral caches) can be pinned to a single territory (US-East) with no automatic cross-region replication.
- How are backups handled? Are incremental snapshots ever replicated outside the pinned territory for durability? If so, can that be disabled?
- Deletion proof: what artifacts can Redwood provide to demonstrate a complete purge? We need timestamps, storage object manifests, and any cryptographic evidence (hashes) tied to KMS key IDs.
- What's your SLA on actually removing tenant data from all systems (runtime KV, persisted snapshots, analytics indices)? We prefer clearly defined windows (e.g., logical delete within X, physical wipe within Y).

Attachments: sample retention policy template we've been asked to compare against (not attached here).

Can you share a short runbook or checklist so we can route this to our auditors? Also looping in Audrey from procurement to track any contract language.

Thanks,

Claire Barnes
Head of Security, FinReg Corp
claire@finregcorp.com

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Claire Barnes <claire@finregcorp.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, rachel_kim@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-18T13:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Territory-bound routing & scrub process — initial questions

Hi Claire — appreciate the clear list. Below are concrete answers and next steps; happy to jump on a 30-min call to walk through.

1) Territory pinning: Dedicated deployments support territory anchoring per cluster. When you request US-East anchoring we create tenant routing rules and placement constraints so primary serving nodes, backups, and snapshots are retained in the pinned territory by default. No automatic cross-region replication is enabled unless explicitly configured.

2) Backups & snapshots: By default, automated incremental snapshots (for fast restore) are stored in the pinned territory. Cross-region replication is an opt-in feature (for geo-DR) and is disabled for pinned tenants unless you request it. We can provide a configuration flag in your Dedicated config to lock replication=false.

3) Deletion proof and artifacts we deliver:
   - Logical deletion event with timestamp (audit-log entry).
   - Storage manifest listing object keys removed (S3 keys or block IDs) with deletion timestamps.
   - Snapshot manifest and snapshot-hash (SHA256) of the final snapshot before purge.
   - Secure-delete job IDs and final status codes from our wipe worker.
   - KMS envelope metadata: key id used to encrypt tenant keys, and log of KMS Decrypt/Generate calls tied to the purge.

4) Typical removal windows (we'll include these in the runbook; negotiable in contract):
   - Logical isolation (deny routing, revoke tokens): immediate (minutes).
   - KV cache eviction and in-memory discard: within 15 minutes of the logical delete event.
   - Snapshot rotation & physical wipe of scheduled snapshots: completed within 72 hours for retention <30d; for immediate purge requests we run expedited purge paths and aim to complete physical wipe within 24 hours.

Attached: dataflow-diagram.pdf (high-level placement for pinned tenants) and redwood-scrub-playbook.pdf (playbook excerpt showing artifacts we produce).

Next steps: we'll assemble a small audit package (templates + example manifests) and circulate to you within 72 hours. If you have a specific format your auditors prefer (CSV manifest, signed PDF, or both) let us know.

Best,

Vanessa Ortiz
Director, Customer Security
Redwood Inference

Vanessa,

Thanks — that level of detail helps a lot. Two quick clarifications before your audit package:

1) Acceptance criteria for 'physical wipe' — our auditors will want a signed, timestamped purge manifest that includes:
   - list of object keys removed
   - deletion timestamps (ISO 8601)
   - snapshot-hash values and snapshot IDs
   - secure-delete job IDs and final status
   - the KMS key-id (not the key material) that wrapped the snapshot/envelope key

2) Chain-of-custody statement — can Redwood provide a short paragraph attesting that no cross-region copy was created for the tenant and that the wipe route executed in the pinned territory? This can be a standard paragraph in the audit package.

If you can include a small template of the purge manifest (CSV) and a sample signed pdf that would be ideal.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — we can hold the procurement amendment until we review the audit package.

Claire

[CC: Audrey Lim, Procurement]
